details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). The brief's done-when says "each test fails without the feature"; test 1 does not fail, it hangs, and the
docstring's "the test's own timeout ends a hang" is untrue: unittest has no timeout and bin/ci sets none. A hang inside the gate is the
worst outcome now that a gate also holds one of three machine slots with no time limit. Size: 15.
evidence: scratch worktree at HEAD with `return open(os.devnull), 0.0` as take_slot's first line;
python3 run1.py <wt>/tests 60  (unittest of test 1 in a new session, killpg after)  ->  HUNG after 60 s
bin/ci:28 lib_tests() { python3 -W ignore::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'; }   (no timeout)
with the feature: python3 -m unittest test_gate_slots -> Ran 4 tests in 6.495s OK
failing_case: take_slot disabled (returns at once). test_with_one_slot_a_second_gate_waits_until_the_first_exits: gate B never prints the waiting
line, runs its HOLD command, and second.stderr.readline() (line 55) blocks until B exits, which is never (the release file is not
written). Seen: still running after 60 s. bin/ci has no test timeout (plain `python3 -m unittest discover`), so `relay gate` would hang
for good instead of going red. Same with wait_for (line 33): if gate A refuses before its command starts, the loop spins forever.
test_a_bad_slot_count_is_refused without the check runs HOLD and dies only at timeout=60, leaving the HOLD shell looping. On any red
run, the cleanups kill the relay processes but never write the release file, so the HOLD loops (sleep 0.05) poll a deleted temp dir forever.
Should: each test fails within a bound (e.g. 30 s) when the feature is off, and leaves no process.
fix_hint: Give wait_for and the waiting-line read a deadline (read stderr in a thread or poll with select and a time limit; wait_for raises after
30 s), and register a cleanup that writes the release file (registered after the kill cleanups so it runs first) in setUp.
pass_cases: 1. take_slot disabled: test 1 fails (assertion or timeout error) within its bound, not hangs; no process of the test is left (the release file is written in cleanup).
2. Feature on: all four tests pass as today (about 7 s).
3. Gate A refuses at once (e.g. a dirty worktree): wait_for raises after its bound instead of looping.
4. RELAY_GATE_SLOTS check removed: test_a_bad_slot_count_is_refused fails and its HOLD command ends (release written in cleanup).
findings.summary: slot tests wait with no bound: with the feature broken they hang the gate instead of failing, and leave polling processes forever

details: CONFIRMED by reading: run() calls subprocess.run(command, ...) with no new session and no signal handling; close_fds defaults to True so
the command never holds the lock; Python's default SIGTERM action ends only the python process. The owner's intent (queue item: "at most
three gates at once", measured: library tests 138 s alone, 489 s with 4+ others) is broken by every killed gate, and the delegation rules
tell runners to wait on and stop processes by their own pid. SIGKILL cannot be caught, so the reachable fix covers SIGTERM, SIGHUP and
SIGINT; passing the lock fd to the command (pass_fds) would also cover SIGKILL but lets a hung command, the usual reason for a kill, hold
the slot for good, so it is not the better fix. Size: 30.
evidence: lib/relay_gate.py:178 done = subprocess.run(command, cwd=worktree, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=sink, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
tests/test_gate_slots.py:76 write(self.release, "go\n")        # lets A's orphaned command end, and B's command go straight through
failing_case: RELAY_GATE_SLOTS=1. Gate A starts bin/ci (about 25 minutes). A runner whose wait ran out does `kill <pid>` on the pid it started
(relay gate's python): python dies on SIGTERM, the lock is released, but bin/ci (started by subprocess.run, its own process, not given
the lock fd) keeps running. Gate B takes the slot at once: two gates run with N=1. test_a_gate_killed_with_sigkill_frees_its_slot shows
it: its own comment says the release "lets A's orphaned command end". Should: stopping a gate stops its command, so the count of
running gate commands never exceeds N.
fix_hint: Start the command with start_new_session=True (Popen), and on SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT (handlers set while it runs) and in the finally
block, kill its process group before the slot is closed. Add the SIGTERM case as a test.
pass_cases: 1. N=1, gate A running its command, SIGTERM to relay gate's pid: A's command is gone (its process group ended) before B's command starts.
2. N=1, gate A ends normally: B starts right after, as today.
3. N=1, gate A killed with SIGKILL: the slot is free (no stale lock), as the brief requires.
4. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) on a waiting gate: it exits without having started its command, and holds no slot.
reason: tests/test_gate_slots.py test_a_gate_stopped_with_sigterm_ends_its_command_before_the_slot_is_free passes, fails on pre-fix code.
findings.summary: killing relay gate frees its slot while its command keeps running, so more than N gates run at once

details: CONFIRMED by reading (run(): check_ready and reusable before take_slot). Not data loss: the merge hook still compares the logged head to
the branch with relay changed and refuses, so it is waste and a misleading log. The window was the run's length before; the wait makes it
failing_case: Three gates hold the slots. In worktree X, gate 1 waits (head H1 read, tree clean). A fixer commits H2 in X meanwhile. When the slot
frees, the command runs H2's tree but the log says `head H1`. Or: the same gate is started twice in X; both wait; the first goes green,
the second still runs the whole gate (about 25 minutes) because reusable() was asked before the wait. Should: after the slot is taken,
check_ready and reusable are asked again.
fix_hint: After take_slot returns, call check_ready again and compare with head (refuse if it moved), then reusable again (close the slot and
return the green log if found).
pass_cases: 1. HEAD moves from H1 to H2 during the wait: the gate refuses (or gates H2), never logs `head H1` for H2's tree.
2. A green log for the same head appears during the wait: the gate frees the slot and reports that log, running nothing.
3. Nothing changes during the wait: the gate runs and logs as today.
findings.summary: head and the reused check are read before an unbounded slot wait, so the gate can run newer code under the old sha or rerun a gate that just went green

details: CONFIRMED by reading; today the only caller (bin/relay cmd_gate) passes no environ, so it is fragile, not wrong. Size: 5.
failing_case: relay_gate.run(wt, environ={**os.environ, "RELAY_HOME": tmp, "RELAY_GATE_SLOTS": "1"}) in-process (as a future test would): the count
is 1 from environ, but the slot files are taken under the live ~/.relay/gate-slots, which tests must never touch. Should: both from environ.
fix_hint: Read RELAY_HOME from env (the dict already built in run) and fall back to relay_config.home_dir() only when it is absent.
pass_cases: 1. run(..., environ with RELAY_HOME=tmp): the slot files are under tmp/gate-slots.
2. run(...) with environ None: ~/.relay/gate-slots (or $RELAY_HOME) as today.
findings.summary: the slot folder comes from os.environ while the slot count comes from the environ argument
